newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends lower, specs continue to liquidate.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends lower, specs continue to liquidate.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended lower and toward the bottom of the day's range for the second day in a row on Tuesday, pressured by continued speculative long liquidation, dealers said.

Benchmark September cocoa fell $17 per tonne on the day, to $1,483, after ranging between $1,504 and $1,481. Second-month December closed $18 lower, at $1,546, while the back months ended down $17 to $19.
Cocoa prices headed lower at the outset, as speculators came in selling after a weak performance in London overnight.
Dealers also noted some origin selling in New York, as producers took advantage of the U.S. dollar's recent strength against many European currencies.
"The strong U.S. dollar has to be discounted in the market and in this case it took the form of origin selling," said one trader.
Additionally, the start of September delivery period on August 18 weighed on the market as traders liquidated or rolled over the spot contract, dealers said.
However, they noted that steady industry-related buying toward the lows buffered the downside and kept September just above chart support at $1,480 a tonne.
"With the selling that was there, we could have been $50 lower," said a trader. "The industry stepped up the pace, which had a neutralizing effect on the liquidation."
News that prospects for the 1997/98 Ivorian crop were favored by rain in late July lent a bearish tone, traders said, although they noted rainfall for the month still lagged behind normal levels.
"It's kind of a double-edged sword," said one trader. "Any rainfall at this point is beneficial, but statistically it's still below normal."

The Ivorian crop analysts noted, however, pod development was unaffected by low rainfall earlier in July as soil moisture had been kept up by cool temperatures, blanket clouds and torrential June rains.

Technically, dealers said today's weak close could weigh on sentiment on Wednesday. On the charts, they said a breach of the $1,480 level in September was likely to trigger sell-stops believed to be building beneath $1,475.
